sehemu: Part III: The Prime Minister, the Cabinet and the Government
maudhui: (1) Notwithstanding the provisions of Article 51, the National Assembly may pass a resolution of a vote of no confidence in the Prime Minister where a motion proposing such a vote is moved and passed in accordance with this Article. (2) Without prejudice to the other provisions of this Article, a motion for a vote of no confidence in the Prime Minister shall not be moved in the National Assembly where - (a) it is not related to the discharge of the responsibilities of the Prime Minister; (b) six months have not elapsed since his appointment; or (c) nine months have not elapsed since a similar motion was moved in the National Assembly and rejected. (3) A motion for a vote of no confidence in the Prime Minister shall not be passed by the National Assembly unless - (a) a written notice signed and supported by not less than twenty percent of all Members of Parliament is given to the Speaker at least fourteen days before the day on which it is intended to be moved; and (b) the Speaker is satisfied that the requirements of the Constitution have been complied with. (4) A motion which complies with this Article shall be presented to the National Assembly as soon as possible in accordance with the Standing Orders of the National Assembly. (5) A motion of no confidence in the Prime Minister shall be passed only if it is supported by a majority of Members of Parliament. (6) Where a motion of no confidence in the Prime Minister is supported by a majority of Members, the Speaker shall submit the resolution to the President and, as soon as possible and in any event within two days after the National Assembly passes the resolution, the Prime Minister shall be required to resign and the President shall appoint another Member of Parliament to be Prime Minister.

(3) A motion for a vote of no confidence in the Prime Minister shall not be passed by the National Assembly unless - (a) a written notice signed and supported by not less than twenty percent of all Members of Parliament is given to the Speaker at least fourteen days before the day on which it is intended to be moved; and (b) the Speaker is satisfied that the requirements of the Constitution have been complied with.
(4) A motion which complies with this Article shall be presented to the National Assembly as soon as possible in accordance with the Standing Orders of the National Assembly.
